about: rasya-taste-v4 footer library: the page's ending (footer.closing: row 1 the close, row 2 the links), dealt as one pick by scripts/footers.mjs from the library's endings (assets/footers/<id>.html, footers.css, footers.js) and the kit's own footer and close types (system.css, starter.html). It replaces the footer and close fields of the one-liner. Rules: references/footers.md. kinds: software, gaming, product (hardware too), service, place, editorial. mood: calm, crisp, playful, editorial (the button moods). nav: the dealt nav types an ending sits well with; buttons: the button looks (buttons.mjs) it sits well with. closeAs: the close type to pass to buttons.mjs --close. attr: the value of data-footer on the footer (the id without footer-, as the kit writes footer-dark as footer--dark). wordmark: the ending sets the brand's name huge (one a page, never two endings in a row). display: the display faces it suits (serif, sans; a pairing's class from library/type.json).

library.name: letterpress wordmark
library.groundNote: the surface grey (the page ground when the last section already sits on the surface); light or dark
library.close: a hairline, then the closing line (the h2) on span-7, a note and the main button on span-4 from column 9
library.footer: one row: the name and one line, the nav's words with Privacy and Terms, the socials; under it the name pressed into the ground, cropped by the page's foot
from: Trove (a footer.design entry): the rule, the serif closing line, the letterpress name

library.name: fading wordmark
library.groundNote: the page ground (an off-white or a dark page)
library.close: a centred closing line, one line under it, the main button
library.footer: a centred row of underlined links (the client's accounts, else the nav's words), the legal line; under them the name huge and pale, fading toward the page's foot, an optional ornament on one letter
from: Cronicle (a footer.design entry): the centred grotesk close, the pill, the underlined links, the pale name with a flower

library.name: split close
library.groundNote: the page ground, or the inverse ground (add footer--dark ground-inverse) on a page whose rhythm has no dark band
library.close: a hairline, then the closing line large on span-7, a note and the main button on span-4 from column 9
library.footer: the kit's columns (the name and one line, two to four link columns) and the legal row
from: Trove's upper half without the wordmark

library.name: outline wordmark that fills
library.groundNote: the inverse ground (dark on a light page, a step off the page on a dark one); data-fill="accent" fills it in a tint of the accent
library.close: the kit's head row: the closing line and one line left, the main button right
library.footer: the kit's columns and legal row; under them the name drawn as an outline that fills from the page's foot as the footer comes up (scrubbed on window.rtMotion; filled under reduced motion)
from: the outlined giant wordmark of SaaS footers (benchmark-saas), given a reason to be there: the fill marks the page's end

library.name: index
library.close: the kit's head row: the closing line and one line left, the main button right
library.footer: the page's sections as a numbered index in the display face (two columns from 1024, two-up on a phone), each row a link to its section; the legal row
library.needs: five to eight sections worth a row; a shorter page deals again with --exclude footer-index

footer-columns.row2: the starter's .closing__links as written: the name and one line, the link columns, the legal row

footer-dark.row2: the starter's .closing__links: the name large top left (.footer__mark), the columns right

footer-statement.row2: the starter's .closing__links on the lit ground (tech only: <html data-ground>)

footer-visit.row2: <template data-part="links-visit">: the address set large with the way there, the hours beside it

close-type.row1: the starter's .closing__cta.close--type as written (the h2, a line, the big button across the .wrap)

close-photo.row1: <template data-part="close-photo">: the head row, then a photograph never used above

close-word.row1: <template data-part="close-word">: the head row, then the name set across the .wrap

close-head.row1: <template data-part="close-word"> without its .close__word: the head row alone (close-photo re-dealt with no photograph left)
